subject: Climate & Environment
title: Sanitation and Dignity
description: A micro-lesson that makes Sanitation and Dignity usable.

hook.text: 3.6 billion people lack access to safely managed sanitation. That is nearly half the world.

buildup.text: Open defecation contaminates water sources and spreads disease across entire communities.

discovery.text: Girls often drop out of school when there are no private toilets — sanitation is a gender issue.

twist.text: Every dollar invested in sanitation returns about $5 in reduced health costs and productivity.

climax.text: India's Swachh Bharat campaign built 100 million toilets in five years — a massive push.

punchline.text: A toilet is not a luxury. It is a lifesaver.

quiz.question: How many people lack safely managed sanitation?

details.summary: Lack of access to toilets and safe sanitation affects human dignity, safety, and health. Women and girls are disproportionately impacted, facing risks of harassment when using open areas and missing school during menstruation. Improving sanitation is a gender equity and human rights issue.
details.whyItMatters: Sanitation is about far more than plumbing. It affects education, gender equality, and personal safety. Addressing it unlocks benefits across multiple development goals simultaneously.
takeaways: Lack of sanitation disproportionately harms women and girls
Open defecation exposes people to disease and personal risk
School attendance improves when sanitation facilities exist

faq.question: How does lack of sanitation affect girls' education?
faq.answer: Without private toilet facilities at school, many girls miss classes during menstruation or drop out entirely at puberty. Studies show that providing clean toilets with menstrual hygiene facilities significantly increases girls' attendance and retention.

faq.question: How many people still practice open defecation?
faq.answer: About 419 million people worldwide still practice open defecation, down from over a billion in 2000. India has made the most progress through its Swachh Bharat mission, but sustained behavior change and maintenance of facilities remain ongoing challenges.
